title: Observability bootstrap for hybrid VPC/on-prem — notes & upgrade plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an opinionated bootstrap + upgrade plan for observability in hybrid private deployments (VPC-connected and on-prem racks). It collects: minimum recommended terraform module wiring, OTEL collector migration notes, Prometheus/Grafana sizing and retention recommendations, log shipping options, cutover/rollback steps, and a short smoke-test checklist.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs and infra engineers running private deployments for customers and partner integrations.
- Scope: on-prem + VPC deployments where we cannot run our hosted telemetry stack. Focus on getting a minimal, secure, maintainable observability stack into customer networks with Terraform modules and a clear upgrade path from older fluentd/log-shipper setups.

High-level architecture (textual):
- Metrics: local Prometheus (node exporters + app exporters) -> remote_write to a hardened metrics ingress (customer-managed or our relay) OR long-term storage (Thanos/sidecar) depending on retention.
- Logs: OTEL collector (preferred) or Fluent Bit as a lightweight forwarder -> buffered file spool -> secure egress to S3-compatible bucket or customer ELK.
- Traces: OTEL collector with sampling + local relay to avoid spikes.
- Dashboards/Alerts: Grafana fronting local Prometheus and remote read endpoints. Alertmanager deployed per-VPC with routing to customer endpoints or webhook relay for Redwood incident ingestion.

Design decisions and rationale (summary):
- OTEL collector preferred over Fluentd/Fluent Bit for unified telemetry (metrics+logs+traces), easier vendor-neutral processing, and future compatibility with our hosted ingest.
- Use Terraform modules as thin wrappers: modules should not bake credentials; expect secrets from vault/KMS provider in the deployment pipeline.
- Default to remote_write with TLS+mutual auth to reduce retention burden on local storage. If offline requirement exists, enable Thanos/Prometheus-HA with object store.

Prereqs before bootstrap: check these in customer environment
- Network: outbound egress allowed to our relay endpoints or S3 targets on ports 443/9000 as required.
- DNS: private DNS entries resolvable for internal service discovery or Consul available.
- IAM/KMS: credentials for object store available via environment/Vault.
- Nodes: at least 1 dedicated monitoring instance for Prometheus, 1 for Grafana, and 1 for OTEL collector in small customers (see sizing).

Terraform module notes (opinionated):
- Module boundary: observability/prometheus, observability/grafana, observability/otel-collector, observability/log-shipping. Keep them composable.
- Inputs (common):
  - namespace (string)
  - prometheus_replica_count (number)
  - grafana_replica_count (number)
  - object_store_endpoint (string)
  - object_store_bucket (string)
  - object_store_cred_secret_name (string)
  - otel_config_map (string or rendered template)
  - scrape_interval (string, default = "15s")
  - retention_hours (number, default = 168)
- Outputs:
  - prometheus_endpoint
  - grafana_endpoint
  - otel_collector_endpoint
- Idempotency and upgrades: modules must attempt no-op if resource already matches. Avoid changing names of k8s objects during upgrades. Use lifecycle ignore_changes for PVC annotations that external tools modify.
- Example minimal invocation (this is a snippet for the terraform root module):

resource "null_resource" "observability_bootstrap_hint" {}
module "prometheus" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//observability/prometheus?ref=main"
  namespace = var.namespace
  prometheus_replica_count = 1
  scrape_interval = "15s"
  retention_hours = 168
  object_store_endpoint = var.object_store_endpoint
  object_store_bucket = var.object_store_bucket
}

module "otel_collector" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//observability/otel-collector?ref=main"
  otel_config_map = file("${path.module}/templates/otel-config.yaml")
  object_store_cred_secret_name = var.object_store_cred_secret_name
}

Notes:
- Always test module changes in a staging VPC first. Keep PRs small (separate grafana/prometheus/collector changes).
- Secret handling: modules reference secret names only; operator pipeline injects secrets from Vault or KMS - never commit creds.

Sizing guidance (small, medium, large):
- Small: 2 CPU, 8GB RAM for Prometheus instance, 2 CPU/4GB for Grafana, 1 CPU/2GB for OTEL collector; retention 7d; suitable for <100k series.
- Medium: 4 CPU, 16GB RAM for Prometheus, replicate with 2 replicas; retention 14d; suitable for 100k–300k series.
- Large: Recommend Thanos sidecar, at least 8 CPU and 64GB RAM split across HA pair and external object store.

Upgrade plan (from legacy fluentd/fluent-bit to OTEL collector + new Prometheus modules):
1) Pre-upgrade verification:
   - Confirm backups of Prometheus data and Grafana provisioning files.
   - Confirm alerting notification targets and escalation policies in a safe staging area.
   - Run smoke exporter that emits synthetic metrics and traces for validation.
2) Deploy OTEL collector in pass-through mode (no processing) alongside existing fluentd for a live-compare (dual shipping for 48–72h).
3) Validate parity: compare logs/metrics/traces received by OTEL vs legacy pipeline. Use sampling-based log checks and histogram differences for metrics.
4) Flip non-critical services to OTEL first. Monitor for missing tags, attribute differences, and ingestion drops.
5) Remove legacy forwarder after 72h of parity and stable checks.
6) Apply Prometheus module upgrade as a rolling update: update scrape config templating first, then increment replica count to create new instances, then retire old ones.

Rolling upgrade considerations:
- Maintain service discovery consistency: keep old SD endpoints in scrape config until new instances appear and are healthy.
- For chart upgrades, bump the chart version in staging and use canary annotation for 10% of nodes.

Log shipping choices and trade-offs:
- Option A (recommended): OTEL collector -> compressed batched upload to S3-compatible bucket -> remote indexing/analysis off-cluster. Pros: vendor neutral, file-level retry, small footprint. Cons: eventual consistency for search.
- Option B: OTEL collector -> direct HTTPS ingestion to customer ELK. Pros: immediate search. Cons: higher tail latency and backpressure risk.
- Option C: Fluent Bit -> Kafka -> downstream consumers. Pros: high throughput. Cons: operational complexity.

Smoke tests and runbook checks (pre-cutover):
- Synthetic metric generator running on a scheduler with expected series count.
- Synthetic log generator writing structured JSON logs with required fields (request_id, svc, severity).
- Alerting test: create test alert that fires and verify Alertmanager -> webhook -> test sink.
- Grafana provisioning verification: stash dashboards in git and ensure provisioning works after Grafana restart.

Cutover checklist (short):
- [ ] Validate network egress and object-store ACLs.
- [ ] Run terraform apply in staging and confirm all resources healthy.
- [ ] Deploy OTEL pass-through and run parity checks 48h.
- [ ] Flip 10% of services to OTEL -> validate.
- [ ] Scale Prometheus replicas and update scrape configs.
- [ ] Retire legacy forwarder.
- [ ] Monitor for 72h.

Rollback plan (if something goes wrong):
- If telemetry loss observed: revert to last working terraform module tag and re-enable legacy forwarder (keep it running until confirm).
- If Prometheus scraping regressions: restore previous scrape_config via terraform state rollback and restart instances.
- Communicate with customer before any data-retention impacting changes (thanos compaction, bucket lifecycle).

Operational runbook snippets (checks to run weekly):
- Check Prometheus TSDB head size and open file handles.
- Check OTEL collector restart rate >1/hr.
- Validate Grafana provisioning sync status and dashboards that have changed.
- Verify object-store bucket size and recent uploads (for logs/Thanos).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide default sample rates for traces in high-traffic customers (proposal: dynamic target sampling tuned by ingest rate).
- Should we provide a lightweight relay (small EC2) as a managed option for customers without a stable egress endpoint?
- Add terraform automated tests (terratest) for each module — backlog ticket required.

Action items (owners):
- [Ava] Create otel-config templates (2 variants: minimal-forwarder, processing-with-drop-policy) — due 2024-10-17.
- [Marcus] Add Terratest harness for prometheus module (initial tests) — due 2024-11-01.
- [Leah] Create Grafana provisioning examples and export baseline dashboards — due 2024-10-24.
- [Omar] Draft runbook play for rollback and incident comms — due 2024-10-09.

Appendix: quick OTEL collector config stub (minimal):
receivers:
  otlp/default:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
      http: {}
exporters:
  otlp/tls_remote:
    endpoint: "remote.ingest.example.com:443"
    tls:
      insecure: false
  file/batched:
    path: /var/spool/otel-batches/logs.ndjson
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp/default]
      exporters: [otlp/tls_remote]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp/default]

Closing notes: this doc is a working capture of our current recommendations. Do not treat as final; iterate rapidly after first two customer installs and update the terraform module READMEs with any gotchas encountered.

If you reference anything from this doc in a customer-facing delivery, please create an internal ticket linking to the deployment and the terraform commit used so we can reproduce the exact config.

-- Ava
